title: DNA extraction from concrete
author: Anders Kiledal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b2i5qcg6
materials: Quantify with Qubit and store at -20°C.

steps.title: Clean sample holder and puck
steps.instruction: Wash the sample holder and puck of the ring and puck mill with soap and hot water, rinse thoroughly, and dry. Rinse the holder and puck twice with 95 % ethanol. Sterilize them under germicidal UV light for 40 min.

steps.title: Break concrete sample
steps.instruction: Roughly break approximately 10 g of concrete with a hammer into pieces small enough to fit into a ring and puck mill or equivalent grinder.

steps.title: Grind concrete to powder
steps.instruction: Grind the broken concrete to a fine powder (typically 1–5 min of grinding). Store the ground powder at –20 °C (or –80 °C) until DNA extraction.

steps.title: Prepare lysis mixture and incubate
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL conical tube add 10 g pulverized concrete, 5 mL 0.5 M EDTA, 150 µL Proteinase K (20 mg/mL), 138 µL 20 % SDS, and 0.2 mL glacial acetic acid. Incubate at 55 °C overnight with gentle rotation.

steps.title: Adjust volume if supernatant low
steps.instruction: If the sample absorbs most of the pre‑treatment solution leaving little supernatant, add 5–10 mL sterile water before vortexing.

steps.title: Vortex sample
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube at maximum speed on a platform vortexer for 10 min (acts like bead beating using the concrete particles).

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 3 min at 5 000 RPM. Transfer the supernatant to a new 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Add binding buffer and silica
steps.instruction: Add 30 mL QGmod to the supernatant. If the solution appears purple (pH > 7.5), adjust pH with acetic acid until it turns yellow (neutral/acidic). Add 125 µL well‑mixed silica suspension and 5 µL yeast RNA (1 mg/mL) as carrier. Mix well and incubate overnight at room temperature with gentle rotation to allow DNA binding.

steps.title: Pellet silica by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 5 min at 5 000 RPM to pellet the silica.

steps.title: First ethanol wash of silica
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant (pour off, briefly centrifuge the tube, and carefully pipette off any remaining Buffer QG). Resuspend the silica pellet in 10 mL 80 % ethanol. Wait ~5 min after adding ethanol before resuspending; if needed, scrape the tube, bang it on the bench, or stir with the pipette tip to break clumps.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash and transfer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 30 min at 5 000 RPM at 4 °C. Decant the supernatant (pour off, pulse‑centrifuge, and carefully pipette off remaining liquid). Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL 80 % ethanol and transfer the suspension to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Pellet silica and dry
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 3 min at 13 000 RPM. Decant or pipette off the supernatant. Air‑dry the silica pellet with bound DNA for ~1 hour at room temperature in a PCR hood.

steps.title: Elute DNA from silica
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 50 µL 10 mM Tris pre‑warmed to 60 °C. Elute for 5 min at 60 °C with gentle rotation. Centrifuge for 3 min at 13 000 RPM and transfer the supernatant (DNA) to a fresh tube. Repeat the elution and combine the eluates.

steps.title: Note on residual silica
steps.instruction: A minuscule amount of silica may remain after elution but should not interfere with downstream applications; any remaining silica can be pelleted if desired.
